items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: There was also another fellow around that I used to listen to a lot... a fellow named Dick Hopkins. I listened to him a lot.

ctx.x: Harold used to play a lot of shows at the Howard Theatre, and at times he would substitute for Earl Hines or some of the other pianists at the Howard Theatre that came to the dances. Because it was kind of proper for the leaders, if they were pianists, to play a few numbers and have a substitute pianist. They would go off the bandstand -- where they would go, I don't know. Then they would come out and maybe play another specialty. Harold showed me a lot about how Teddy Wilson was playing, because he played that…
There was also another fellow around that I used to listen to a lot, although he played more like Earl Hines. He's still around, a fellow named Dick Hopkins. I listened to him a lot.
Then there was another guy. His name was Clyde Wright.
